full_judgment: 2. The suit was for a declaration that the treatment of the suit properties at Schedules I, II, III and IV to the plaint as abandoned properties is wholly without jurisdiction, void initio, collusive, malafide, fraudulent, that the schedule properties are not abandoned properties and that the plaintiff is the sole owner of the schedule properties and also for a decree for khas possession of Schedule I-IV properties in favour of the plaintiffs. The suit was filed on 11-7-85. The defendant-appellants took 6 (six) months'' time to file a written statement wherein it was contended that during the liberation movement and afterwards the whereabouts of the plaintiffs were not known and the suit properties were taken over as abandoned properties. The plaintiff himself did not depose in the suit. His constituted attorney deposed as PW 1 on 15-4-92, 9-1-3 and on 23-1-93 when he was partly cross-examined by the learned Advocate for the defendant-Ministry of Works. Several dates were fixed thereafter for further cross-examination of PW 1, but the defendant-appellants did not complete the cross-examination. Ultimately, the trial Court fixed a date for hearing the arguments and on an adjourned date on 24-1-93 the trial Court heard the arguments for the plaintiff, but the defendant-appellants' learned Advocate did not argue on that date or on any subsequent date. At last on 28-4-93 the trial Court delivered the judgment decreeing the suit.
